![San Diego Zoo Safari Park Autumn Festival](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/styles/hero_with_nav_gradient/public/hero/SP20251_8140_Autumn-Festival_web-landing-hero_1920x1067.jpg?itok=LtaTvVxr)

October 4–5, 11–12, 18–19, and 25–26

# AUTUMN FESTIVAL

We’re celebrating the return of the season of color during Autumn Festival, every Saturday and Sunday in October. Amazing wildlife, special entertainment, and delicious culinary comforts await! Join us to create heartwarming memories and enjoy good ol’ fashioned family fun.

## SAFARI BASE CAMP

![Safari Park Radio 197.2 ](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/autumn_festival_sp_radio_thumb.png)

### Safari Park Radio

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. (continuous)

The Safari Park’s own radio station broadcasts an upbeat, modern country soundtrack that’s perfect for fall days. Listen for interactive trivia games and “Did You Know?” segments about the fascinating conservation efforts you make possible to save, protect, and care for local wildlife through our [Southwest Conservation Hub](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/conservation-hub/southwest).

## CONDOR RIDGE

![Safari Parker character waving.](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/autumn_festival_safari_parker_thumb.png)

### Safari Parker

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 1, 2, 3 and 4 p.m. (30 minutes)
- Condor Trail, Burrowing Owls

Safari Parker, our explorer and adventurer extraordinaire, will entertain everyone with facts about [burrowing owls](https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/burrowing-owl), how they’re vital to their delicately balanced ecosystem, and how your support is helping this species thrive through our [Southwest Conservation Hub](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/conservation-hub/southwest).

## NAIROBI VILLAGE

![two people in blue button up shirts smiling and holding instruments](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP2024_6230_Autumn-Festival-ash-meadows_web-thumb_668x540.jpg)

### Ash Meadows

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 1:15, 2:15, 3:15, and 4:15 p.m. (30 minutes)
- Nairobi Village, Oasis on the Rocks

This talented duo features a unique musical combination of acoustic guitar and mandolin, filling the autumn air with their relaxing sounds.

![two performers dressed as scarecrows on stage](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP2024_6230_Autumn-Festival-jamboree_web-thumb_668x540.png)

### Autumn Festival Jamboree

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 2, 3, 4, and 5 p.m. (30 minutes)
- Nairobi Village, Village Playground

Join our scarecrow hosts for a good ol’ fashioned country dance party that’s sure to get your toes tappin’ and your boots scootin’!

![Two scarecrow characters. ](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/autumn_festival_scarecrow.png)

### Not-So-Scary Scarecrows

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 2:45 – 5:45 p.m. (continuous)
- Nairobi Village, Village Playground

Look for our happy-go-lucky scarecrows as they show off their juggling and bouncing skills in their own silly ways.

![Family walks in a hay maze](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/autumn_festival_maze_thumb.png)

### A-MAZE-ing Autumn Adventure

- Daily
- Park open to Park close
- Nairobi Village, Village Playground

Young wildlife explorers will love navigating this fun, walk-through maze. As they make their way through the twists and turns, they’ll discover clues to identify Southwest wildlife.

![Barn owl band.](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/autumn_festival_barn_owls.png)

### The Barn Owls

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 2:30, 3:30, 4:30, and 5:45 p.m. (30 minutes)
- Nairobi Village, Village Playground

Our talented trio of country musicians will keep everyone entertained with their down-home and bluegrass musical stylings.

![Lanterns floating on water at the Safari Park](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP2024_6230_Autumn-Festival-reflections_web-thumb_668x540.png)

### Reflections

- Saturdays and Sundays
- 6:45 p.m. (7 minutes)
- Nairobi Village, Lagoon Loop

Take a musical and colorfully lighted journey around the world as our lantern ceremony concludes your autumn evening with a celebration of people, wildlife, and the planet we all share.

## Culinary Offerings

![Churros and teriyaki pork chop sandwich](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP2025_8140_Autumn-Festival-retail-specials_web-thumb_668x540.png)

### Savor Autumn’s Tastiest Treats

- Daily
- Various Locations

During Autumn Festival, savory delights await throughout the Safari Park. Delectable fall entrees include the **Teriyaki Pork Chop Sandwich** at Mombasa Cooker, **the Surf and Turf Burrito** at Mawazo Kitchen, and **Crab Cakes** at Oasis on the Rocks. For those with a sweet tooth, **Caramel Apple Churro Fries** are available at various locations.

![3 festive fall drinks for autumn festival](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP2025_8140_Autumn-Festival-retail-specials-drinks_web-thumb_668x540.png)

### Fall for Refreshing Beverages

- Daily
- Various Locations

Thirsty? Autumn favorites and drink specials include the **Stone Fruit Spice Cocktail** at Oasis on the Rocks, the **Caramel Apple Arctic Blast** at Kalahari Cupboard, the spirit-free **Appletini Float** at Kibo Cones, the **Autumn Pumpkin Churro Sundae** at Kalahari Cupboard and Okavango Outpost, and the **Prickly Pear Margarita Cocktail** at Oasis on the Rocks and Max’s Hideout.

# Butterfly Jungle

Separate ticket purchase required

Immerse yourself in the vibrant world of pollinators as you explore Butterfly Jungle. Once a year, this aviary transforms into a world of color. As hundreds of butterflies fly around guests and explore the colorful foliage and flowers in their habitat, you'll snap amazing photos and experience wonder while discovering the important role butterflies play in nature.

Admission to Butterfly Jungle is not included with a Safari Park admission ticket or membership, which is required for guests ages 3 and older. A separate Butterfly Jungle Safari ticket purchase is required for all guests, including members and children ages 1 and older. Children younger than 1 require a complimentary infant pass, which can be reserved at the Butterfly Jungle Safari ticket booth.

[_Learn more about butterflies with this field guide._](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/sites/default/files/2023-03/Butterfly%20Jungle%20field%20guide_SP23-digital.pdf)

**For more information, see** [**Butterfly Jungle FAQ**](https://sdzsafaripark.org/butterfly-jungle#faq) **at the bottom of this page.**

![butterfly](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/butterfly-thumb3.png)

### Butterfly Jungle Safari

[BUY NOW](https://tickets.sandiegozoo.org/webstore/shop/viewitems.aspx?cg=webstoresdp&c=6214146)

- All ages
- $18 per person (ages 1 and older)

Children younger than 1 require a complimentary infant pass
- Daily, March 21 through April 12, 2026
- Hidden Jungle

Become immersed in the vibrant world of pollinators as you explore the Safari Park's Butterfly Jungle. Once a year, this aviary transforms into a world of color. As butterflies fly around you, snap amazing photos and experience wonder while discovering the important role butterflies play in nature.

This 20-minute experience includes nectar to offer the butterflies while you explore their habitat. Guides and wildlife care specialists will be available inside the Hidden Jungle aviary to enhance your experience throughout your visit. A separate admission ticket or membership is required for Safari Park entry.

[_Learn more about butterflies with this field guide._](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/sites/default/files/2023-03/Butterfly%20Jungle%20field%20guide_SP23-digital.pdf)

_Infants under the age of 1 are free and require a complimentary infant pass, available on grounds at the Butterfly Jungle ticket booth, first come, first served._ _Due to fire safety codes, we are limited to 5 carried infants (under the age of 1) in the Butterfly Jungle experience at the same time._

_We will do our best to accommodate guests up to 15 minutes past their reserved time. Beyond 15 minutes, arrivals cannot be accommodated; original tickets are non-refundable, and a new purchase is required._

![Monarch butterflies](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/butterfly-thumb2_668.png)

### Protecting California's Butterflies

[LEARN MORE](https://sdzsafaripark.org/protecting-californias-butterflies)

San Diego County is a biodiversity hotspot and home to a dazzling array of wildlife, including 150 different species of butterflies! Find out how your visits and support help safeguard the future for California's butterflies through our [Southwest Conservation Hub](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/conservation-hub/southwest).

### Butterfly Jungle FAQ

When is Butterfly Jungle at the Safari Park?

Butterfly Jungle at the Safari Park takes place from March 21 through April 12, 2026.

What are the hours for Butterfly Jungle?

The Butterfly Jungle experience is open daily from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. between March 21 and April 12, 2026.

Is Butterfly Jungle included with Safari Park admission and/or membership?

Butterfly Jungle tickets are purchased separately from and are not included with Safari Park admission and/or membership. All Butterfly Jungle visitors ages 1 and older, including members, must purchase a ticket for Butterfly Jungle Safari. For children younger than 1, please request a complimentary infant pass at the Butterfly Jungle ticket booth upon arrival. Safari Park admission is separate and required.

I am a member. Do I need to purchase a timed ticket for Butterfly Jungle Safari to experience Butterfly Jungle?

Yes. All guests, regardless of age (including members and nonmembers), will need a date- and time-specific Butterfly Jungle Safari ticket to visit Butterfly Jungle. Safari Park admission or membership is separate and required.

What programs and Safaris include Butterfly Jungle?

The 20-minute Butterfly Jungle Safari is the only butterfly-centric experience in 2026. We encourage you to reserve another one of our [safari adventures](https://sdzsafaripark.org/safaris) to enhance your visit!

Are strollers permitted inside Hidden Jungle?

No, strollers are not permitted inside of Hidden Jungle. Stroller parking is available outside of the aviary.

## Welcome to the Burrowing Owl Cams!

**Burrow In**

San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance is home to a pair of burrowing owls in an off-view breeding area. However, you can observe these fascinating birds on this live cam—which provides views above ground, as well inside the birds' underground burrow, where eggs are incubated and chicks are raised. It's a wonderful opportunity to learn more about this charismatic species!

**Why We Care**

The western burrowing owl is at risk of going locally extinct in San Diego County. To help reverse the decline, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance's Burrowing Owl Recovery Program is working with partners on a comprehensive, multifaceted approach to address burrowing owl ecology and conservation practices in Southern California. These efforts include reengineering habitat to make it suitable for burrowing owl colonization through providing artificial burrows that mimic natural burrows, as well as adding California ground squirrels to the landscape, which dig burrows the owls can “reuse.” Many burrowing owls have been banded for identification purposes, while some owls get tiny solar-powered GPS telemetry “backpacks” so researchers can track them over time.

**Field Trip**

Visitors with internet access can become community scientists and help us classify field photos taken by motion-activated cameras set up outside a burrowing owl den in Otay Mesa, California. The project, called [Wildwatch Burrowing Owl](https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/sandiegozooglobal/wildwatch-burrowing-owl), helps researchers suss out the complexities of feeding, mating, and other burrowing owl behaviors with the help of our volunteers.

[Learn more about burrowing owls](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/species/burrowing-owl)

[Read burrowing owl stories](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/story-hub)

## Welcome to the Elephant Cams!

You are watching archived footage of the elephant herd at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park, recorded at an earlier date. The live cam is temporarily unavailable due to construction on the new Denny Sanford Elephant Valley—the largest project in the San Diego Zoo Safari Park's 50-year history—which will completely reimagine the heart of the Safari Park, bringing our community into the epicenter of our global conservation efforts for elephants.

When completed, the reimagined Elephant Valley will provide enhanced opportunities for guests to connect with the herd in new and engaging ways. Through the course of construction, elephant habitat viewing locations will be modified and may at times be limited.

Just as their counterparts do on the African savanna, the elephants at the Safari Park live in a social group called a herd, made up of females and their offspring. The leader of the herd—known as the matriarch—is usually the oldest and most experienced female in the group. She keeps the younger elephants in line and teaches them how to behave in elephant society.

The Safari Park’s elephant habitats spread out over six acres and are divided into two main yards, providing all the elephants with opportunities for social interaction. With eight African elephants, there’s always something happening!

[Learn more about elephants](https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/elephant)

[Read elephant stories](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/story-hub)

Meet our elephants:

## Mkhaya "Kaia"

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Safari Park, September 26, 2018

**September 2018 weight (at birth):** 281 pounds

Wildlife care specialists at the Safari Park received a big surprise when they came in to work on the morning of September 27, 2018, and saw that 28-year-old Umngani had given birth to a healthy 281-pound female calf—the biggest calf ever born at the Safari Park (calves usually weigh 200 to 268 pounds at birth). By late morning, with the baby appearing healthy and bonded to her mother, wildlife care staff offered the pair the opportunity to move into a larger area of the habitat with Umngani's other three offspring. The new calf was also introduced to 8-year-old male Emanti and 11-year-old female Phakamile, or "Kami." The other elephants rushed to meet the new baby, touching and smelling her with their trunks, all under the watchful eye of her protective mother.

## Umzula-zuli "Zuli"

**Sex:** Male

Born: Safari Park, August 12, 2018

**August 2018 weight (one day after birth):** 277 pounds

Just before midnight on August 12, 2018, in the final hours of World Elephant Day, mother Ndulamitsi gave birth to a male calf called Umzula-zuli, or "Zuli." The next day, Zuli was greeted by the herd's other elephants, who gathered around him—eager to touch him, trumpet, and smell him with their trunks.

## Swazi

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Kruger National Park, South Africa, approx. 1991

**Weight:** 6,800 pounds

Swazi has been the dominant female in the herd since she arrived. Named in honor of Swaziland, she is the now the largest female in the herd. Any ruckus in the herd and Swazi comes charging over to see what’s going on. Swazi gave birth to her first, long-awaited calf—eMacembe, a male—on April 12, 2010, and a female, Qinisa, on August 28, 2012. Wildlife care specialists suspect that Swazi's vision is not as acute as the other elephants; she is often startled by the less-dominant animals, sometimes even the calves.

## Umngani

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Kruger National Park, South Africa, approx. 1990

**Weight:** 6,250 pounds

Umngani (OOM-gah-nee), whose name means “friend” in Siswati, is the mother of Mkhaya, a new female calf born in September 2018, as well as Khosi, Ingadze, and Inhlonipho. Umngani is curious and eagerly participates in care sessions, often roaring at wildlife care specialists if her session ends too soon. Umngani has the longest tusks in the herd, and her ears are often flared out as if she is listening. As beautiful as she is, though, she is also one of the messiest elephants in the herd. You can tell which wildlife care specialists have been working with her; they are frequently spackled with wet mud from her drippy trunk!

## NdLulamitsi "Ndula"

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Kruger National Park, South Africa, approx. 1990

**Weight:** 6,400 pounds

Ndlulamitsi has a great relationship with her wildlife care specialists and often approaches them to solicit a rubdown. She can often be seen in the water and taking mud baths to cool down. Ndula became the first mom of the herd when she gave birth to Vus’musi; son Lutsandvo was born in 2010. In August 2018, she gave birth to son Umzula-zuli. You can identify Ndula, whose name means “taller than trees,” after her great height, by her right tusk, which curves underneath her trunk.

## Khosi

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Safari Park, September 11, 2006

**November 2012 weight:** 3,206 pounds

Khosi (KO-see) is short for a name that means "heart of a queen" in Siswati and was named in recognition of Yvonne Larsen, former president of the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Board of Trustees. Khosi can frequently be seen watching over her younger siblings.

## Phakamile "Kami"

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Safari Park, September 19, 2007

**November 2012 weight:** 2,685 pounds

Phakamile's name means "noble strength" and honors the longtime support of Audrey Steele Burnand, whose first name means the same. Kami is a great swimmer, is very energetic, and is good at balancing on logs or rocks. Kami's right tusk is very short; a tusk injury required a pulpotomy.

## Qinisa

**Sex:** Female

**Born:** Safari Park, August 28, 2012

**June 2013 weight:** 694 pounds

Qinisa is mother Swazi's second calf. Qinisa's name is a Siswati word that means to act with energy, act determinedly, fulfill one’s word, or speak the truth. The name is pronounced "EEN-EE-seh," with a tongue pop instead of a q sound. Her name is very fitting, as she is definitely full of energy.

## Welcome to the Giraffe Cam  Supported by ABCMouse

**Giraffes, rhinos, and more! Enjoy this view of The Savanna from Kijamii Overlook at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. And help us save giraffes by joining our community science program,** [**Wildwatch Kenya**](https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/sandiegozooglobal/wildwatch-kenya) **.**

## Welcome to the Platypus Cam!

You're watching a live stream from the Safari Park—the only platypus outside of Australia. This unique marsupial serve as an ambassador for the species outside of their native Australia and communicate the importance of fresh water for both humans and wildlife. We’re honored to be entrusted with their care.

Day and night are reversed in our habitat because platypus are most active at nighttime. But when it's night in San Diego, the lights come up, and you can see them in their daytime pool.

[Learn more about platypuses](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/species/platypus)

[Read platypus stories](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/story-hub)

# Dining at the Safari Park

## Dining Category

![Mkutano House Dining Room](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/mkutano-house-dining.jpg)

### Mkutano House

[Learn More](https://sdzsafaripark.org/node/653)

- Location: Elephant Valley

Share bold dishes highlighting flavors from around the world, sip on delicious beverages, and connect with the elephant herd like never before—all from Mkutano House in the heart of Elephant Valley.

Vegetarian and gluten-free options are available.

_Reservations recommended. An 18% gratuity charge to be added to check for parties of 7 or more._

![Ono Lounge seating](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/ono-lounge-dining.jpg)

### Ona Lounge

- Location: Elephant Valley

Look out over Elephant Valley with sweeping views from Mkutano House’s prestigious second floor as you sip on refreshments crafted with premium spirits sourced from local distilleries from across Africa.

_Additional cover charge is required._

![Tu Grill Outside Dining](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/tu-grill-dining.jpg)

### Tu Grill

- Location: Elephant Valley

Satisfy your larger-than-life hunger with tasty skewers, a variety of sides, refreshing smoothies, and more without missing a moment with the elephant herd.

Vegetarian and gluten-free options are available.

![The Sheared Sheep](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/ShearedSheepDining_thumb_0.jpg)

### The Sheared Sheep

- Location: Walkabout Australia
- [Menu](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/dining/sheared-sheep/menu)

Come hang out with a nearby tree kangaroo and a cassowary, and enjoy a salad, a wrap, or one of our Australian-inspired snacks—along with specialty cocktails or a refreshing draft/craft beer.

![barking deer bbq & beer](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/7043_SP24_Barking-Deer-BBQ-Update_WEB-Thumb_668x540_0.jpg)

### Barking Deer

- Location: Safari Base Camp
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/barking-deer/menu)

Stop in for our delicious pizza! Wash down your satisfying meal with our refreshing draft and craft beer selections or soft drinks.

Looking for something sweet? Choose from a wide variety of Dippin’ Dots flavors, our Dippin’ Dots Root Beer Float, and our delectable Dippin’ Dots Cookie Dough Toffee Delight.

![Thorntree Terrace](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/Thorntree_thumb_0.jpg)

### Thorntree Terrace

- Location: Safari Base Camp
- [Menu](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/dining/thorntree/menu)

Enjoy a delicious meal beside our beautiful thorn tree. You’ll find breakfast items like bagels and cinnamon rolls, along with sandwiches, burgers with fries, salads, fish and chips, Kid’s Meals, and refreshing beverages—including a variety of soft drinks and draft/craft beer. Vegetarian and gluten-free options are available.

![Mombasa Cooker](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/MombasaCooker_thumb_0.jpg)

### Mombasa Cooker

- Location: Nairobi Village
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/mombasa-cooker/menu)

Dine outdoors on the water in an African-themed village, surrounded by waterfowl and other wildlife. Enjoy hand-battered chicken tenders plates, burgers with fries, salads, Kid’s Meals, and a variety of beverage options, including draft/craft beer and soft drinks. Vegetarian and gluten-free options are available.

![oasis on the rocks exterior](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP24_AT5316_oasis-on-the-rocks_web-landing-thumb_668x540_LC.jpg)

### Oasis on the Rocks

- Location: Nairobi Village
- [Menu](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/dining/oasis-on-the-rocks/menu)

Located in the heart of Nairobi Village, Oasis on the Rocks features specialty cocktails, and draft/craft beer, and soft drinks.

![Max's Hideout](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SP25_8883_Maxs-Hideaway_web_thumb_668x540.jpg)

### Max's Hideout

- Location: Safari Base Camp
- [Menu](https://sdzsafaripark.org/dining/maxs-hideout/menu)

Unwind with refreshing specialty cocktails like Max's Margarita, our twist on a prickly pear margarita named after the iconic salmon-crested cockatoo. It’s even garnished with his favorite snack—red grapes. Plus, pair sweet and salty treats with a unique selection of local craft beer.

While you’re here, grab fun keepsakes to take home with Max-themed t-shirts, hats, and water

bottles.

![Okavango Outpost](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/OkavangoOutpost_thumb.jpg)

### Okavango Outpost

- Location: African Outpost
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/okavango-outpost/menu)

After exploring the savanna on Africa Tram, visit Okavango Outpost for a delicious meal. We offer comforting pasta, satisfying sandwiches, and vibrant salads. Complete the experience with our delectable churro sundae for dessert.

![Mawazo Kitchen](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/Mawazo_thumb_0.jpg)

### Mawazo Kitchen

- Location: African Woods
- [Menu](https://sdzwa.org/dining/mawazo/menu)

Dine with a view as you enjoy delicious South of the Border-themed entrees, chicken tenders, fries, salads, Kid’s Meals, and refreshing beverages, including soft drinks and draft/craft beer. This outdoor dining facility is conveniently located between Benbough Amphitheater and Mawazo Playground. Vegetarian and gluten-free options are available.

![Kibo Cones & Snacks](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/Kibo_thumb_0.jpg)

### Kibo Cones & Snacks

- Location: Nairobi Village
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/kibo-cones/menu)

Looking for something sweet in the heart of Nairobi Village? Enjoy our soft-serve ice cream, ICEEs, and floats! We offer a variety of snacks, including pretzels, churros, and hot dogs.

![Safari Coffee Outpost](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/SafariCoffeeOutpost_thumb_0.jpg)

### Safari Coffee Outpost

- Location: Safari Base Camp
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/safari-coffee-outpost/menu)

Start your day off with a selection of specialty coffee drinks, warm mini doughnuts, snacks, and cold drinks, as you browse among the unique items at our adjacent Plant Trader gift shop.

![Macan Market](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/Macan_thumb_0.jpg)

### Macan Market

- Location: Tiger Trail
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/macan-market/menu)

Relax at our beautiful Sambutan Longhouse, and select from a light luncheon menu that includes snacks, draft/craft beer, and soft drinks, while you watch tigers watching you!

![Lion Camp Slush & Snacks](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/LionCamp_thumb.jpg)

### Lion Camp Slush & Snacks

- Location: Lion Camp
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/lion-camp-slush-and-snacks/menu)

Watch the Safari Park’s hot-air balloon rise above the savanna, as you cool off with a build-your-own slush, paired perfectly with your favorite snacks—from churros to hot dogs—or enjoy a refreshing soft drink or draft/craft beer.

![Rift Sand Bar](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/RiftSandBar_thumb_0.jpg)

### Rift Sand Bar

- Location: The Grove
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/rift-sand-bar/menu)

Relax and enjoy the beautiful view of the African Plains from the top of the elevator deck, along with a refreshing snack, some popcorn, a pretzel, a soft drink, or draft/craft beer.

![Tucker Truck](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/TuckerTruck_thumb_0.jpg)

### Tucker Truck

- Location: Walkabout Australia
- [Menu](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/dining/tucker-truck/menu)

Located in Walkabout Australia between the platypus habitat and the Bonsai Pavilion, Tucker Truck serves up tasty french fry cones, snacks, and cold drinks.

![Raptors Nest](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/RaptorsNest_thumb_0.jpg)

### Raptor's Nest

- Location: The Grove

Hang out and enjoy the beautiful view of our Flightline Safari landing area and our Roar & Snore camp area. At Raptor’s Nest, you’ll find snacks, soft drinks, draft/craft beer, wine, and specialty cocktails.

![Kalahari Cupboard](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/KalahariCupboard_thumb_0.jpg)

### Kalahari Cupboard

- Location: Nairobi Village
- [Menu](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/dining/kalahari-cupboard/menu)

Before you stop by the Petting Kraal, visit Kalahari Cupboard for an Arctic Blast with blended soft-serve ice cream, or an ICEE and snacks, and enjoy a view of the waterfall near the wooden bridge.

![Congo Kitchen](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/CongoKitchen_thumb_0.jpg)

### Congo Kitchen

- Location: Safari Base Camp
- [Menu](https://www.sdzwa.org/dining/congo-kitchen/menu)

Conveniently located near a triangle of gift shops, just steps from Nairobi Village, Congo Kitchen offers nachos, popcorn, snacks, cold drinks, and draft/craft beer.

![ShopZoo logo - boy and girl wearing San Diego Zoo Safari Park merchandise](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/9067_ShopZoo_Elephants_footer_ad-780x962.jpg)

Dining

# Mkutano House

[All Dining Locations](https://sdzsafaripark.org/dining)

Step into the heart of the savanna and connect with the elephant herd like never before—all from the comfort of Mkutano House in the heart of Elephant Valley. Mkutano is Swahili for “gathering with purpose.”

Share delicious dishes from the innovative, globally inspired menu with your loved ones and sip on handcrafted cocktails featuring premium spirits sourced from local distilleries across Africa.

Vegetarian and gluten-free options are available.

_Reservations recommended. An 18% gratuity charge to be added to check for parties of 7 or more._

# The Watering Hole at Kijamii Overlook

[All Dining Locations](https://sdzsafaripark.org/dining)

The Watering Hole will no longer be accepting restaurant reservations beginning February 17, 2026. From all of us at the Safari Park, we are grateful for the bites, sips, and views we’ve shared here together.

This venue is still available for [private and catered events](https://events.sandiegozoo.org/venues/kijamii-overlook). When not in use for special events, it will be open for you to enjoy snacks, cocktails, and other refreshments.

_To book your celebrations and other events at the Watering Hole at Kijamii Overlook, visit_ [_Wild Events_](https://events.sandiegozoo.org/) _._

**Join us at the brand-new full-service restaurant Mkutano House, opening March 5 in the heart of Elephant Valley.** Here you can experience all the same culinary creativity you love while enjoying unparalleled views of the African elephant herd.

## A Whole New Perspective

Watch our special drone show over San Diego Bay amplifying the opening of the all-new [Denny Sanford Elephant Valley](https://sdzsafaripark.org/elephant-valley).

Hundreds of drones seamlessly shared the extraordinary world of elephants with our local community, key partners, and wildlife allies from around the globe.

Experience African elephants for yourself when you visit [Elephant Valley](https://sdzsafaripark.org/elephant-valley), and learn more about how we’re securing their future for generations to come through our [Savanna Conservation Hub](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/conservation-hub/savanna).

# THIS IS HUGE

## The All-New Experience, Now Open

When you come face-to-face with the largest land animals on Earth, it’s not just your mood that shifts—it’s your perspective. Suddenly, everything feels bigger. You don’t just witness an elephant’s majesty; you share common ground.

At Denny Sanford Elephant Valley, you’ll experience what it’s like to coexist with this magnificent species. Walk alongside the herd, connect with them on an entirely new scale, and become part of a movement working to secure their future for generations to come. Here, you’ll feel inspired to stand for something larger than yourself, as we all work together to protect these gentle giants.

Elephant Valley was made possible through the generosity of more than 5,200 donors. We extend our heartfelt thanks to all whose support helped bring this new experience to life.

_Elephant Valley is included with San Diego Zoo Safari Park admission. See below for additional enhanced experiences._

### WATCH THE TV SPOT

Step into the heart of the savanna and discover what awaits at the new Denny Sanford Elephant Valley.

![Safari Park](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/body_side_image/MODULE_IMAGE_1_1035x716.jpg)

### A World of Wonder

Step into a one-of-a-kind world of wonder and majesty, where your loved ones, our elephant family, and the global community come together as one.

![Elephant and child](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/body_image/MODULE_IMAGE_2_1035x716.jpg)

### Like Never Before

Get closer than ever before, observing elephants and their behavior in a truly immersive experience.

![Two looking at Elephant](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/body_side_image/MODULE_IMAGE_3_1035x716.jpg)

### Walk Alongside Giants

Enjoy a front row seat as elephants roam the sprawling savanna landscape and feel what it’s like to become one with the herd.

![Elephant and child](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/body_image/MODULE_IMAGE_4_1035x716.jpg)

### Memories Made to Last

Watch with delight as elephants of all ages swim, splash, play, and cool off in Mugurr West pond on a hot summer day.

Image

![Orange graphic divider](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/divider-2.png)

![Elephant Valley herd](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/meet-the-herd.png)

### Meet The Herd

Meet the Safari Park’s biggest family. From the matriarch’s leadership to the fearlessness of the youngest, discover the family dynamics of this multi-generational herd of African savanna elephants. Experience their unique personalities and larger-than-life adventures as they explore the day together at Elephant Valley.

[Read more](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/story-hub/meet-the-herd-elephant-valley)

Image

![Orange graphic divider](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/divider-3.png)

![Mkutano House interior](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/two-column-1.png)

![Plates of food](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/two-column-2.png)

![Mkutano House logo](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/mkutano-logo.png)

### DINE amongst giants

Take a moment to relax, reconnect, and share a meal in the heart of Elephant Valley.  Mkutano House offers an unforgettable, open-air dining experience with stunning views of Mugurr West Pond and the surrounding savanna. Enjoy wood-fired entrees, shareable plates, and more as the ‘joy of gathering’ inspires meaningful connections.

[Read More](https://sdzsafaripark.org/dining)

# Elephant Valley Opening Celebration

March 5–8, 2026

# Entertainment Schedule

## Friday, March 6 & Saturday, March 7 Performances

![Kora Instrument](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/21-strings.jpg)

### 21 Strings

- Ticketing Plaza, Near Map Locator 6

Enjoy the sounds of the kora, a traditional West African instrument.

- Ticketing Plaza \| 9 a.m., 10 a.m., and 11 a.m.
- Near Map Locator 6 \| Noon and 1 p.m.

![Safari Parker](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/safari-parker.jpg)

### Safari Parker

- Ticketing Plaza, Nairobi Walk

Our explorer says hello and shares amazing elephant facts.

- Ticketing Plaza \| 9:30 a.m., 10:30 a.m., and 11:30 a.m.
- Nairobi Walk \| 12:30 p.m., 1:30 p.m., 2:30 p.m., and 3:30 p.m.

![whimsical wildlife characters](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/whimsical.jpg)

### Whimsical Wildlife Characters

- Nairobi Village/Base Camp

Take photos with and meet our fanciful wildlife puppets.

- Nairobi Village/Base Camp \| 9 a.m.–Noon, 1–4 p.m.

![Savanna Sounds](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/savanna-sounds_0.jpg)

### Savanna Sounds

- Village Base Camp Stage

Showcase of music and dances of East Africa.

- Village Base Camp Stage \| 10 a.m., 11 a.m., Noon, and 1 p.m.

![Amazing Acrobats of Tanzania](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/acrobats.jpg)

### Amazing Acrobats of Tanzania

- Village Base Camp Stage

High-energy fun with amazing acrobats from East Africa.

- Village Base Camp Stage \| 2 p.m., 3 p.m., and 4 p.m.

![Musician with drum](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/music-south-africa.jpg)

### Music of South Africa

- Village Playground

Interactive musician with songs of South Africa.

- Village Playground \| 10 a.m., 11 a.m., and noon

![Rhythms of Africa](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/rhythms.jpg)

### Rhythms of Africa

- Village Playground

Experience interactive songs and dances with our talented musician.

- Village Playground \| 1:30 p.m., 2:30 p.m., and 3:30 p.m.

![Tropical Tunes](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/tropical-tunes.jpg)

### Tropical Tunes

- Near Map Locator 6

Relax to the amazing sounds of steel drums.

- Near Map Locator 6 \| 9:30 a.m., 10:30 a.m., 11:30 a.m., and 12:30 p.m.

![cheetah](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/wildlife-care-talks.jpg)

### Wildlife Care Talks and Wildlife Experiences

- Cheetah Run near Lion Camp \| 10:00 a.m.

![Animal](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/journey-into-wild.jpg)

### Journey Into the Wild

- Benbough Amphitheater

- Benbough Amphitheater in Gorilla Forest \| 1:00 p.m.

![Mkutano House exterior](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/coming-together.jpg)

### Coming Together in Mkutano Park

**Come explore with us! Make meaningful nature connections and feel the power of community in conservation.**

Community Art

How will you leave your print as we work together to help all life thrive?

Community Partner Art Project

View art created by San Diego Zoo Safari Park education partners.

Living in Harmony with Nature

Make your own bee water station.

Nature Observers

Discover the stories wildlife tell.

Trunks & Tales Story Time

10:30 a.m. and Noon

Join the Herd

Create an elephant that is uniquely you!

Activities open:

- Friday, March 6: 9:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
- Saturday, March 7: 9:30 a.m.–4 p.m.

School & Youth Programs

# Field Trip Reservation Form

**All schools in San Diego County only should fill out the form below to request their field trip dates to the San Diego Zoo Safari Park.**

To be eligible for field trip rates for San Diego County schools, schools must reside in San Diego County and are able to abide by [SDZWA Education Program policies](https://sdzsafaripark.org/field-trip-policy/southern-ca).

All other student groups [click here](https://sdzsafaripark.org/student-youth-groups). If you would like to book a field trip to the San Diego Zoo , please [click here](https://zoo.sandiegozoo.org/student-youth-groups).

Additional Information

Lunch storage is available at the Safari Park in the Log Ring, located outside the Park entrance. Please note, the cubbies in the Log Ring do not lock. No coolers/food storage containers larger than a 6-pack size are permitted on grounds.

Alternatively, if you would like to pre-purchase meal vouchers for $23.00 each, please list the number you would like to purchase here.

Number of Meal Vouchers?

$23.00 per meal voucher

Private Africa Tram

Tours available Monday-Friday. Each tram accommodates up to 70 people and costs $350 per tram. Join us for a private narrated, 25-minute expedition viewing our diverse wildlife who live in the savanna habitats, giving you a chance to connect with wildlife on a closer level. Limited departures available at this special rate reserved for school-affiliated groups. Must reserve one month in advance. Cancellation fee applies.

Number of Requested Trams?

$350 per tram

School & Youth Programs

# Field Trip Reservation Form

**All schools in Southern California only should fill out the form below to request their field trip dates to the San Diego Zoo Safari Park.**

To be eligible for field trip rates for Southern California schools, schools must reside in Los Angeles, Orange, San Bernardino, Imperial, or Riverside County, and able to abide by [SDZWA Education Program policies](https://sdzsafaripark.org/field-trip-policy/southern-ca).

All other student groups [click here](https://sdzsafaripark.org/student-youth-groups). If you would like to book a field trip to the San Diego Zoo, please [click here](https://zoo.sandiegozoo.org/student-youth-groups).

Student & Youth Groups

# School Field Trip Policies

[All Student & Youth Groups](https://sdzsafaripark.org/student-youth-groups)

### **San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Youth Group and “Other Students” Field Trip Policy**

- **SDZWA Youth Groups and Other Student Groups are defined as** students visiting for non-curriculum based excursions. Students must comprise a minimum of 50% of group to qualify for Youth Group rates. All chaperones must be at least 21 years of age.
- **“Other Students” are defined as** Schools outside Southern California and in US national and international locations.

**All Youth Groups and “Other Students”** wishing to participate in any SDZWA Youth Group Programs must request a reservation first.  Reservation requests are subject to prior approval by SDZWA. SDZWA only books directly with schools, youth group organizations, travel tour operators and authorized school representatives, not third-party proxies.

**Note:** SDZWA reserves the right to grant reservations, revoke reservations, and make exceptions and/or changes in their sole opinion

### **Homeschool/Charter School Policy**

Homeschools/charter schools must meet youth group and “other student” group requirements to participate in the SDZWA Field Trip program.

Additional options for homeschools/charter schools include:

- Purchase a membership and come at your leisure
- Visit during Kids Free Month in October where all kids aged 11 and under are free, no reservation required. NOTE: Youth over the age of 11 do not qualify for Kids Free promotion.

### **Sibling Policy**

Siblings are defined as any child not enrolled in the specific grade level that has RSVP’d for the Field Trip.

Sibling participation in SDZWA field trips are not permitted.  Any exceptions to this policy must be requested in advance and are subject to prior approval by Education Department SDZWA Yyouth Ggroup sales Ddepartment. If approved for exception, siblings aged 3 and older must pay the posted admission rate or use a membership to gain entry.

### **Field Trip Reservation Policy**

Reservations are required at least 4 weeks in advance. Limited spaces are available, first come first served. Reservations are only considered confirmed with an SDZWA provided confirmation number. Any requests made within 4 weeks of the group visit date is subject to a late fee of $75 booking fee.

**Head Count:** Participant count section of confirmation page must be completed before entry and the entire group on the reservation must enter at the same time. Different entry times are unable to be accommodated for one reservation.

**Tickets:** Admission Tickets will only be provided once group is present, counted and paid in full. Tickets may not be repurposed or up charged.

**Payments:** Only ONE form of payment per reservation on day of the field trip will be accepted. Payment must be in the form of a credit card, purchase order (PO), or cash. Once paid, no refunds will be issued, and all payments are final. Field trips are a rain or shine event.

**Applying Membership Towards Field Trip Admissions:** Valid memberships can be used in conjunction with field trip reservations.  All passes must be collected before the check-in process, separated into “adult” and “child” bundles, and presented along with the participant count section and form of payment at time of group check-in. Members must show ID and membership card upon entry.

### **Group Size Requirements**

- A Minimum of 15 participants per group is required.
- 72 participants per classroom per reservation is allowed.
- A Maximum of 150 participants per school, per reservation is allowed unless special arrangements are made in advance via .
- All Groups sizes of 500 or more are subject to approval by SDZWA Youth Group Department.

### **Chaperone Policy**

- A Minimum of 1 chaperone :6 students, grades 1-10 - required.
- Chaperones exceeding ratio - charged at applicable rates\*
- Chaperone ratios over 1 chaperone:1 student - not eligible for the Field Trip Program rates.
- Teachers and aides must be included in the chaperone count.
- All chaperones must be at least 21 years of age.

##### \*Youth & Student Attendees with disabilities who require additional chaperone support can be accommodated above ratios, please inquire at time of booking.

# School Field Trip Policies

[All Student & Youth Groups](https://sdzsafaripark.org/student-youth-groups)

### San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Public/Private School Field Trip Policy

**SDZWA Field Trips are defined as** classroom students visiting for curriculum-based learning, guided by an accredited or credentialed teacher.  Classroom students must comprise a minimum of 50% of group to qualify for Field Trip rates.  Classroom students must be enrolled in the same classroom/grade level. Teachers are defined as the lead educator ultimately responsible for the classroom students.

**All public or private schools** wishing to participate in any SDZWA Field Trip Program must set up an account first, including their National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) ID.  Accounts are subject to prior approval by SDZWA. SDZWA only books directly with schools and authorized school representatives, not third-party proxies.

**San Diego County** public or private schools wishing to participate in the free San Diego County Schools Field Trip Program must reside in San Diego County and be listed on the CA Department of Education Directory.

**Southern California** public or private schools that are outside of San Diego County wishing to participate in the So Cal discounted SDZWA Field Trip Program must be listed on the CA department of Education Directory. Only one visit per classroom per year per facility (Zoo & Safari Park) will be permitted.

Field trip rates are made possible by generous donors and intended specifically for approved school field trips.  SDZWA does not allow organizers to misrepresent the intent of the field trip program or upcharge for access to or service for field trips.  Groups found up charging will be immediately cancelled, and their account terminated. Paid group (e.g. youth groups, third party providers, non-school groups) organizers should coordinate groups through the main SDZWA Call Center and will be subject to standard group rates.

**Note:** SDZWA reserves the right to grant reservations, revoke reservations, and make exceptions and/or changes in their sole opinion.

### **Homeschool/Charter School Policy**

Homeschools/charter schools must meet Public/Private school group requirements to participate in the SDZWA Field Trip program.

Additional options for homeschools/charter schools include:

- Purchase a membership and come at your leisure (educational resources are provided at no cost online and some homeschool/charter programs provide a stipend that can be applied towards membership purchase)
- Visit during Kids Free Month in October where all kids aged 11 and under are free, no reservation required.

### **Sibling Policy**

Siblings are defined as any child not enrolled in the specific grade level that has RSVP’d for the Field Trip.

Sibling participation in SDZWA field trips are not permitted.  Any exceptions to this policy must be requested in advance and are subject to prior approval by Education Department. If approved for exception, siblings aged 3 and older must pay the posted admission rate or use a membership to gain entry.

### **Field Trip Reservation Policy**

Reservations are required 4 weeks in advance. Limited spaces are available, first come first served. Reservations are only considered confirmed with an SDZWA provided confirmation number.

**Head Count:** Participant count section of confirmation page must be completed before entry and the entire group on the reservation must enter at the same time. Different entry times are unable to be accommodated for one reservation.

**Tickets:** Admission Tickets will only be provided once group is present, counted and paid in full. Tickets may not be repurposed or up charged.

**Payments:** Only ONE form of payment per reservation on day of the field trip will be accepted. Payment must be in the form of a credit card, check with ID, purchase order (PO), or cash. Once paid, no refunds will be issued, and all payments are final. Field trips are a rain or shine event.

**Applying Membership Towards Field Trip Admissions:** Valid memberships can be used in conjunction with field trip reservations.  All passes must be collected before the check-in process, separated into “adult” and “child” bundles, and presented along with the participant count section and form of payment at time of group check-in. Members must show ID and membership card upon entry.

### **Group Size Requirements**

- A Minimum of 15 participants per group is required.
- 72 participants per classroom per reservation is allowed.
- A Maximum of 150 participants per school, per reservation is allowed.

**Note:** Only one visit per classroom per year per facility (Zoo & Safari Park) is permitted.

### **Chaperone Policy**

- A Minimum of 1 chaperone :6 students, grades 1-10 - required.
- Chaperones exceeding ratio - charged at applicable rates\*
- Chaperone ratios over 1 chaperone:1 student - not eligible for the Field Trip Program rates.
- Teachers and aides must be included in the chaperone count.
- All chaperones must be at least 21 years of age.

##### \*Students with disabilities who require additional chaperone support can be accommodated above ratios, please inquire at time of booking.

July 29, 2022

# Global Tiger Day

Join us Friday, July 29 at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park's Tull Family Tiger Trail, as we celebrate Global Tiger Day. Come face-to-face with critically endangered Sumatran tigers, hear from the experts who care for them, and discover how your support is helping secure their future. With fun surprises throughout the day, this will be a special experience for the whole family!

### Ask the Experts!

- Select times, 10 a.m.–3 p.m
- Tull Family Tiger Trail

Enjoy exclusive opportunities to meet with wildlife care specialists and conservation scientists. Learn more about tigers and the incredible conservation efforts you make possible at the Safari Park and around the world.

- 10 a.m. – Wildlife Care Specialist Talk
- 12:30 p.m. –  Wildlife Care Specialist Talk
- 2:45 p.m. – Wildlife Care Specialist Talk
- Select times – Conservation Scientist Chat

### Activities Table

- Select times, 10 a.m.–3 p.m.
- Tull Family Tiger Trail

Get your paws dirty with tiger arts and crafts to celebrate Global Tiger Day.

### Wall of 1,000 Wishes

- Tull Family Tiger Trail

It takes a global alliance to save Sumatran tigers—and it starts with you! As an ally for wildlife, add your hopes to the wall of 1,000 wishes for tiger conservation. Then, show your support—and your stripes—by getting your face painted like a tiger.

### Meet a Horticulturist

- Select times, 11:15 a.m.–1:15 p.m.
- Tull Family Tiger Trail

Meet our wildlife care experts, and hear how they care for more than 3,700 species and 1.3 million plants at the Safari Park. Discover how we sustainably farm food for the wildlife we care for, manage our own on-site water reclamation and recycling facilities to irrigate landscapes, and help endangered plants thrive through our accredited gardens.

### Tiger Tales

- 11 a.m., 1 p.m., and 2 p.m.
- Tull Family Tiger Trail

Join us throughout the day for an enchanting story-time escape. Wildlife Explorers of all ages will love these tiger stories.

### Fuel Your Adventure

- Safari Base Camp—Thorntree Terrace

Hungry? Fuel up for your big day with delicious Asian-inspired treats at Safari Base Camp’s Thorntree Terrace.

### Cart Safari Asia

- Reservation required

Enjoy a 60-minute guided tour of the Safari Park’s sprawling Asian savanna habitats, led by one of our knowledgeable guides. As you explore these habitats, your safari guide will share stories about the wildlife in our care and how your support impacts conservation worldwide. Step off the cart for an up-close look at the wildlife you love, and snap some photos as you enjoy this unique Safari Park experience. Space is limited, so [make your reservation](https://tickets.sandiegozoo.org/webstore/shop/viewItems.aspx?cg=webstoresdp&c=spkcs21) ahead of time.

### Deluxe Cart Safari

- Reservation required

Travel the world without leaving San Diego. Our expert guides will take you on a deluxe safari cart, transporting you around  the savannas of Africa and Asia. Space is limited, so [make your reservation](https://tickets.sandiegozoo.org/webstore/shop/viewItems.aspx?CG=webstoresdp&C=spdlcsf) ahead of time.

### Deluxe Flightline Safari

- Reservation required

With a spectacular bird’s-eye-view of our Asian and African savannas—teeming with rhinos, giraffes, cape buffalo, and other wildlife—Flightline Safari is the ultimate adventure for those looking to soar with excitement. You’ll experience breathtaking views as you travel nearly two-thirds of a mile on a zip line, high above the wildlife below. [Make your reservation today](https://sdzsafaripark.org/safaris/flightline-safari).

### Show Your Stripes

- Thursday, July 28–Sunday, July 31
- Select retail locations

Save 20% and share your love for tigers by purchasing a T-shirt or tote bag for Global Tiger Day. Each sale funds critical conservation efforts worldwide.

### Adopt a Tiger

[ADOPT](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/adopt/sumatran-tiger)

Your symbolic [adoption of a Sumatran tiger](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/adopt/sumatran-tiger) fuels conservation work supporting tigers and other magnificent species across the globe.

# Grant-funded Programs

Classes Available to Grades K–5 in Title 1 schools in the following districts: Alpine Union, Cajon Valley, Chula Vista, Coronado, Dehesa, Jamul-Dulzura, Lakeside, La Mesa/Spring Valley, Lemon Grove, Mountain Empire Unified, National Elementary, San Diego Unified, Santee, San Ysidro, and South Bay Union.

**For more information about any of these programs, please visit bookeo.com/sdzed-programs, or for more information, please email** [**EducationZoo@sdzwa.org**](mailto:EducationZoo@sdzwa.org) **.**

##### For Kindergarten–Grade 1 classes at Title I schools in San Diego County

#### San Diego County Students

Blending social and emotional learning, and Next Generation Science Standards, this two-part program includes a visit to your classroom and a field trip to the Zoo for your class, to inspire empathy for wildlife. Students will learn what animals need to survive, what body parts help with survival, and will be able to commit to at least one empathy-related conservation action. Bus transportation reimbursement is provided.

##### For all Grade 2 classes in San Diego County

#### Habitat Heroes

For over 50 years, the San Diego Zoo has offered a free field trip to all second-grade classes in San Diego County that includes an up-close wildlife encounter and a guided bus tour of the Zoo. This NGSS-aligned program lets students be scientists and discover the variety of plants and animals from habitats here in San Diego and around the world. Students are challenged to make observations, discover patterns, and compare wildlife across habitats.

##### For all Grade 3 classes at Title I schools in San Diego County

#### What's the Buzz?

Students participate in hands-on learning, understanding the broader impact of habitat changes on plants and pollinators due to urbanization and the importance of habitat restoration. In this two-part program, our goal is to empower students, showing them that even small actions can positively impact local habitats.

##### For Grade 4 classes at Title I schools in San Diego County

#### Sensational Scientists

This three-part program aims to inspire students to be scientists, as they observe and document the various ways wildlife use their senses to navigate and understand their world. Zoo educators, Dr. Zoolittle, and wildlife ambassadors will engage students in hands-on activities in the classroom program, Zoo field trip, and virtual classroom program. Throughout all program components, students will explore how plants and animals experience the world through their senses, and how their sensory structures help them to accomplish many key aspects of survival.

##### For Grade 5 classes at Title I schools in Southern San Diego County

#### Wildlife Rangers

Fifth-grade classes at select districts in San Diego County will become community scientists, as they learn the important role that wildlife rangers play in protecting our local habitats, including our unique biodiversity hotspot right here in San Diego! This two-part program includes a classroom visit and a field trip to a local wildlife refuge. Students will practice scientific skills used by wildlife rangers and conservation specialists—locally and around the world—to protect wildlife.

# Guest Code of Conduct

San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance (SDZWA) is dedicated to providing a safe and welcoming, family friendly environment for its members and guests. We value and seek the strengths of human variety with respect to ethnicity, age, culture, gender, personal values and beliefs, physical abilities, religion, and sexual orientation. We are committed to a world where all life thrives.

To promote a positive, enjoyable experience for all our team members, guests, and wildlife in our care, we have established this guest code of conduct. SDZWA requires all individuals on grounds to follow these rules and guidelines, and adhere to local, state, and federal laws. We expect guests to show common courtesy to fellow guests and our team members by showing respect to others and contributing to a welcoming and family friendly environment. We ask all guests to contribute by refraining from using profanity or engaging in unsafe, illegal, disruptive, or offensive behavior; to act responsibly; and respect the rights and dignity of others.

SDZWA reserves the right to prohibit any activity that it determines may be harmful or disruptive, in its sole and absolute discretion. SDZWA further reserves the right to deny admission, prevent entry, or require a person already admitted to leave any SDZWA property, facility, or any party thereof, without refund, liability, or compensation, or other appropriate action(s) for failure to comply with any of these rules, for unsafe, illegal,or offensive behavior, to ensure safety, security, or order, or if we consider that thecircumstances otherwise so require, in our sole and absolute discretion.

Proper attire, including shoes and shirts, must be worn at all times. SDZWA reserves the right to deny admission to or remove any person wearing attire that we consider inappropriate or attire that could detract from the experience of other guests.

Please be courteous and kind—and enjoy your visit with San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance.

LIST OF PROHIBITED ITEMS:

- Disposable straws
- Cigarettes, e-cigarettes, vapes and marijuana. We are a smoke-free environment
- Alcohol and illegal substances
- Weapons of any kind to include replicas and toys
- Disruptive items such as drones, laser pointers, noise makers and sporting equipment
- Any transportation device not otherwise approved as a mobility device per SDZWA’s ADA guidelines
- Inappropriate or offensive attire. Proper attire, including shoes and shirts must be worn at all times
- Animals other than trained service animals
- Coolers larger than 12” by 12”
- Glass bottles or containers
- Costume masks or costume/clothing deemed by SDZWA management that too closely resembles an employee uniform
- Professional photographers with professional cameras or recording equipment, who are visiting the San Diego Zoo and/or Safari Park with the intent to take photographs or recordings of people, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance properties, or icons for professional purposes. Permission must be requested in advance and prior arrangements must be made with the appropriate San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance representatives. Permission for any recordings or broadcasts on the premises are within the sole discretion of San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance.

# Guest Services

Save time: [pre-purchase your tickets online](https://www.sdzsafaripark.org/tickets), then bypass the front gate when you arrive, and come right in to start your Safari Park adventure!

**The San Diego Zoo Safari Park is a smoke-free facility.**

**Stroller Rentals:** Strollers are available for rent on a first-come, first-served basis near the entrance. Availability and price subject to change without notice. You are welcome to bring your own stroller.

**Rental Prices:**

Stroller single: $16

Stroller double: $20

**Wheelchair and ECV Rentals:** Manual wheelchairs and ECVs (Electronic Conveyance Vehicles) are available for rent on a first-come, first-served basis near the entrance. Availability and price subject to change without notice. You are welcome to bring your own wheelchair or ECV. Rental ECVs cannot be accommodated on our shuttles or Africa Tram. Please refer to our [Guide for Guests with Disabilities](https://sdzsafaripark.org/guests-disabilities) for more information.

**Rental Prices:**

Manual wheelchair:  $16

ECV:  $60

**Automated Teller Machines (ATMs):** For your convenience, ATMs are located at the front entrance (just before the entrance turnstiles), at Guest Services, and on the elevator deck.

**Kennels:** There are no kennels provided for pets, comfort animals or emotional support animals. We do not offer kennel service at either park. If you will require kennel service during your visit, please use the Contact Us link at the bottom of this page, so we may provide a list of local kennels.

**Lost and Found:** Please visit Guest Services if you have lost an item or child. Open daily to closing. After closing, you can inquire about lost items by leaving a voicemail at 619-231-1515, ext. 5267 or via email at [splostandfound@sdzwa.org](https://sdzsafaripark.org/splostandfound@sdzwa.org).

**First Aid:** Please visit Guest Services.

**Information, Inquiries Regarding Public Transit, and Plant Identification:** Please visit Guest Services.

**San Diego Zoo Safari Park App:** Navigating the Safari Park has never been easier! Follow the map to find directions to your favorite animal at either the Safari Park or the San Diego Zoo. The GPS-enabled app map will keep you on the right path. [**Download the app for iPhone or Android.**](https://sdzsafaripark.org/plan-your-visit)

# Guests with Disabilities

[Download San Diego Zoo Safari Park Accessibility Guide (PDF)](https://sdzwa.org/sdzwa-accessibility-guide)

[Website Accessibility Statement](https://www.sdzsafaripark.org/accessibility-statement)

**Jambo! The San Diego Zoo Safari Park welcomes all guests. We have several services to help all our guests enjoy their visit.**

We have a map that marks the stops for our ADA (American with Disabilities Act) shuttle. These maps are also available at our ticket booths and at Park Base. Restrooms and services—including many of our Safaris—are wheelchair accessible. [Wheelchairs and motorized scooters are available for rent on a first-come, first-served basis near the entrance at Safari Outfitters.](https://sdzsafaripark.org/guest-services) Please refer to our Accessibility Guide for more information. The minimum age requirement to operate an Electric Conveyance Vehicle (ECV) is 18 years old.

[Click here to download our Accessibility Map (PDF)](https://sdzwa.org/park-ada-map-print)

Guests who have difficulty standing in line at the Africa Tram may request an “Easy Access Pass” at the Tram Host podium, across from the Africa Tram ticket booth. The attendant on duty will provide a return time for the group based on the length of the line. Guests may continue exploring and return at their assigned boarding time. Up to four additional members of the guest’s party may accompany a guest with a disability.

We welcome guests with disabilities who choose to bring their trained service animal into the Safari Park. Emotional support animals as well as companion, comfort, or service animals in training are not allowed entry into the Safari Park. Our guidelines for service animals can be found by accessing the San Diego Zoo Safari Park Accessibility Guide.

Please see our Accessibility Guide (click the link at the top of this page) for Frequently Asked Questions and more detailed Safari Park information for guests with disabilities.

**Mobility Assistive Device Policy**

San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance is dedicated to providing all of its guests with equal enjoyment of the wonderful experience offered by its parks: the San Diego Zoo and the San Diego Zoo Safari Park.

The safety of our visitors is extremely important to us. The parks are primarily pedestrian environments. By “pedestrian,” we mean any individual who moves within walking areas with or without the use of walking-assistive devices such as crutches, leg braces, wheelchairs, etc. Park attendance is often at high capacity, resulting in busy pedestrian pathways. Our goal is to maintain a safe pedestrian traffic flow for all visitors while allowing for use of mobility-assistive devices that do not fundamentally alter the nature of the experience the parks provide.

In order to maintain a safe pedestrian environment and the desired pace and flow of visitor traffic, the parks do not allow guests to bring or use most wheeled vehicles within the grounds. Bicycles, tricycles, scooters, skateboards, roller skates, and similar modes of transportation are not allowed within the grounds. The parks allow strollers as well as the following mobility-assistive devices for use by guests with disabilities: wheelchairs, electric scooters, and Segways®. All Segways entering the parks must be operated in “turtle” mode so as not to disrupt the desired pace of the visitor traffic at the parks and disturb other guests.

The Safari Park provides accommodations to people who need mobility assistance while on our grounds. Shuttle service is available for guests with limited mobility and guests who use wheelchairs, running on a continuous loop stopping at Guest Services and Okavango Outpost. The Park also offers a limited number of wheelchairs and electric scooters for rent. In addition, the Park provides free admission for a personal attendant/caregiver to accompany a guest who requires such help to access the Park's public programs, activities, and facilities.

San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance reserves the right to modify this policy at any time as it deems appropriate.

**Additional Information**

[San Diego Zoo Safari Park Accessibility Guide](https://sdzwa.org/park-ada-guide)

For general questions not answered here, please email accessibility@sdzwa.org, or call 619-231-1515 after 8:30 a.m. PDT.

October 13, 2025

# Indigenous Peoples' Celebration

Join the San Pasqual Band of the Kumeyaay Nation as they host Indigenous Peoples' Celebration for the community at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. All are welcome to this joyous celebration of the Kumeyaay people and the Indigenous community, their commitment to wildlife, and their culture.

## Schedule of Events

### Blessing Ceremony

- 10 a.m.
- Benbough Amphitheater

Opening remarks from tribal elders, prayer songs, and special guests gather to bless and begin this special event.

### Telling of the Creation Story

- 11 a.m. & 2 p.m.
- Mawazo Restaurant

With an audience Q & A to follow.

### Indigenous Artisans Exhibition

- 11 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.
- Nairobi Village Walkway

### Environmental Wellness Ambassadors

- 11 a.m. - 3:00 p.m.
- Mombasa Pavilion

Traditional and educational activities for the whole family.

### Bird Singing Groups

- 10:30 a.m. - 3 p.m.
- Benbough Amphitheater

### Live Music

- 11 a.m. - 3:00 p.m.
- Near Barking Deer Pizza

### Conservation Science Talks

- Varying times between 11:00 a.m. - 3:00 p.m.

Discover the incredible species that call the Southwest home. At varying locations throughout the Safari Park our teams of experts will share how we're saving wildlife, and how allies like you can help.

### Culinary Offerings

- 11 a.m. - 4 p.m.
- Throughout the Safari Park

Specialty menu offerings will be available throughout the Park.

### Trail Trek

- Ages 6 & up
- Free; limited capacity -- reservations required.\*
- 11 a.m.
- Map Marker #19 at Condor Ridge

Join us for a 1.2-mile hiking adventure connecting the stories of the Kumeyaay people with San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance’s Southwest conservation hub. Explore Condor Ridge and the World Gardens, and venture into the Safari Park Biodiversity Reserve, a 900-acre protected natural habitat that is home to over 200 native species. Members of the San Pasqual Band will share stories of the original stewards of the San Pasqual Valley. Learn about our work with conservation partners to conserve native wildlife, including burrowing owls, desert tortoises, California condors, and the coastal sage scrub ecosystem.

\*This hike is free. Space is limited; reservations are required by calling 619-718-3000. Ages 6 and older.

_This 1.2 mile hiking adventure lasts about 2 hours and is of moderate difficulty. The first half of the hike is uphill, the second half is downhill. A restroom stop is available about 20 minutes into the hike; there are no other restroom stops along the route. There will be stops for water and snacks (provided) at the one-quarter and halfway points, and at the conclusion of the hike. Please wear comfortable walking shoes!_

### Closing Ceremony

- 4 p.m.
- Benbough Amphitheater

## Learn More

### San Pasqual Band of Mission Indians

[Learn More](https://www.sanpasqualbandofmissionindians.org/)

Learn more about the San Pasqual Band’s history, culture, and thriving community.

### Southwest Conservation Hub

[Learn More](https://sandiegozoowildlifealliance.org/conservation-hub/southwest)

Efforts to protect wildlife, ecosystems, and people are stronger when we honor the knowledge and expertise of those in our community, including Indigenous peoples.

At the San Diego Zoo Safari Park, you’ll get up close to some super cool animals, like rhinos, giraffes, kangaroos, zebras, and so many more—all in their own natural habitats. Plus, every visit supports wildlife conservation.

**So**[**get your tickets**](https://sdzsafaripark.org/tickets)**now, then come and Join the Herd!**

August 13–15

# KENYA DAYS

Join us as we celebrate the wildlife, sights, sounds, and tastes of this amazing African country.

## Entertainment

The following are included with Safari Park admission or membership:

![Safari Park Radio - 197.2 FM](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/%20SafariPark%20_Radio_0.jpg)

### Safari Park Radio 197.2

- 9 a.m. to Park close
- Base Camp

The modern, pop/rock and hip hop-influenced music of today’s hottest Kenyan artists will fill the air of Safari Base Camp.

![Kenyan Drummer. ](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/summer_safari_drummer_thumb_0.png)

### Kenyan Drumming

- 1:45, 2:45, 3:45, and 4:45 p.m. (20 minutes)
- Mawazo Playground

Our Kenyan drummer will entertain, interact with, and educate guests on the fun, importance, and history of the drum in East Africa.

![Safari Parker waving. ](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/kenya_day_safari_parker.png)

### Safari Parker

- 2:45 p.m. at Elephant Valley (40 minutes)
- 3:45 p.m. at Kilima Point (40 minutes)
- 4:45 p.m. at Lion Camp (40 minutes)
- 5:45 p.m. Base Camp to Flightline (40 minutes)
- Varies

Our adventurer and explorer extraordinaire will interact with guests, giving them insight into the work San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance does in Kenya while educating them on Kenyan wildlife and horticulture in the Park’s care.

![Kenyan traditional storyteller.](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/page_list_item/kenya_day_storyteller.png)

### Kenyan Fables

- 3, 4, 5, and 6 p.m. (25 minutes)
- Village Playground

Storytelling and creation of fables is a popular and ancient art in Kenya. Our storyteller will perform an interactive tale like those created in East Africa.

![ShopZoo logo - boy and girl wearing San Diego Zoo Safari Park merchandise](https://sdzsafaripark.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/9067_ShopZoo_Elephants_footer_ad-780x962.jpg)

Youth Programs

# Conservation Corps

[All Youth Programs](https://sdzsafaripark.org/youth-programs)

## Conservation Corps Details

Age Range: High school students

Calling all teens! Are you interested in making a difference for wildlife? Then Conservation Corps at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park is for you. The Conservation Corps is a hands-on program that offers high school students the opportunity to learn about conservation and environmental issues while developing their communication and critical thinking skills. Participants will also have the opportunity to give back to the community by participating in conservation projects in San Diego County, allowing students to learn from and network with experts and professionals in various conservation fields. Please note, there are no animal handling or interaction opportunities within this program.

- Conservation Corps will meet on select Saturdays beginning in September and ending in December.

- Students must be currently enrolled in 10th, 11th, or 12th grades.

- Interested applicants must attend a **mandatory** information session with a parent or guardian. Applications will only be available to those who attend an information session.

- If selected, applicants must be available for an interview held at the Safari Park in early September.

- Thanks to a generous donation, this program is free of charge to accepted students for the Fall 2025 session.

Please [click here](https://forms.office.com/r/km6nNuGKAC) to sign up for **one** of our information sessions to learn more and receive an application. You will receive more information regarding your information session before the scheduled date.

- Wednesday, August 27, 2025: Zoom Information Session, 5:30 pm – 6:30 pm

- Deadline to register for this information session is Monday, August 25, 2025 by 11:59 pm

- Saturday, August 30, 2025: Zoom Information Session, 10:00 am – 11:00 am

- Deadline to register for this information session is Thursday, August 28, 2025 by 11:59 pm

## Questions? Email EducationPark@sdzwa.org or Call (760) 738-5057

Participant testimonials:

- _“This gave me a better understanding of what conservation actually looks like and really opened my eyes to all the different pathways/careers that exist within conservation. ”_

- _“I was able to have meaningful discussions with other people my age who were also passionate about conservation.”_

(760) 738-5057

# Kids Free

Calling all Wildlife Explorers! October is Kids Free month at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park, and youths 11 years and younger receive free admission all month long (with an adult). Youths can connect with their wild side by meeting wildlife, while discovering the wonders of nature through play and exploration.

_For more information about Kids Free, see our_ [_Seasonal Event FAQs_](https://zoo.sandiegozoo.org/help-center#seasonal-events) _._

### Autumn Festival

- Saturdays and Sundays in October

Come join all the autumn festive fun as the San Diego Zoo Safari Park celebrates the season of color with special activities, entertainment, and culinary comforts. Learn more [here](https://sdzsafaripark.org/autumnfestival).

### Kids Free FAQ

What is Kids Free October?

Each year, from October 1–31, in honor of our Zoo’s founding, youths 11 years of age and younger are granted free entrance to the Zoo and Safari Park when accompanied during their visit by an adult age 18+ with a vaild form of entry (membership, admission ticket, U.S. military ID, etc.). Youths ages 2 and younger are always free. Children ages 15 and younger must be accompanied by an adult 18+ with a valid form of entry during their visits to the Zoo and the Safari Park.

What ages qualify for Kids Free?

During the month of October, youths 11 years of age and younger get free admission to both the San Diego Zoo and Safari Park, when accompanied by an adult. During the entire year, youths age 2 and younger are admitted free, when accompanied by an adult.

Does the accompanying adult have to purchase an adult ticket for Kids Free?

Adults must use their valid active membership, pass, or admission ticket to enter the Zoo or Safari Park at any time during operating hours—including during Kids Free month. During the month of October, youths 11 years of age and younger are free.

What is the allowable Kids Free adult-to-child ratio?

During our October Kids Free event, each ticketed supervising adult may bring up to six (6) youths (ages 11 and younger) free.

Can I use my active duty military discount during Kids Free?

Valid active duty military receive complimentary admission for themselves. Please bring your valid active duty CAC card with you. During the month of October, your children ages 11 and younger are free.
